changes.before: If label in Labels.kt becomes private, can Main.kt still call it?
changes.after: Packages organize code names, while visibility rules decide which code may use them.

before: The helper below belongs to package study, so import study.label makes its function available by its short name. A package declaration—not a folder name alone—determines the qualified name. Imports do not fetch code.

Save the helper in Labels.kt and compile it together with Main.kt. A public top-level function can be imported here. If it becomes private, another file cannot call it, even in the same package. internal instead means visibility within a compilation module, not package privacy.
```kotlin
package study
fun label(): String = "review"
```

Complete local Kotlin/JVM example; the app itself does not execute it:
```kotlin
import study.label

fun main() {
    println(label())
}
```
Expected output or behavior: review. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Create a second public helper and compare public, private and internal deliberately. You may trace it without a Kotlin compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: A package groups code under a name. The declaration `package study` gives label the full name `study.label`. An import lets another file use the shorter name label. It does not download or create the helper code.

Visibility controls access. A public top-level function can be used from another file. Top-level private limits it to its own source file. Internal allows access within the module, the group of files compiled together, rather than only within one package.
The screen shows `review`. Main.kt imports the public helper and calls it.
A package comes from the package declaration, not just the folder name. An import cannot bypass a private declaration. Keep both source files available when building this example.

before.question: If label in Labels.kt becomes private, can Main.kt still call it?
choices: Yes: every file in a directory is one file.
No: top-level private is limited to its source file.
before.explanation: A separate file cannot access the private top-level declaration through an import.

after.question: Make label private in Labels.kt. Can Main.kt still call it?
choices: Yes, because files in one folder count as one file.
No, because a top-level private function is limited to its own file.
Yes, because imports bypass visibility rules.
after.explanation: Main.kt is a different source file. Its import cannot access the private top-level function in Labels.kt.
